newsitem.title: USA: Emerging debts becalmed, eyes on Brazil swap deal.
newsitem.headline: Emerging debts becalmed, eyes on Brazil swap deal.

text.p: Emerging market debts were unchanged to firmer Monday in line with U.S. Treasuries.

Brazil's debt swap, which would allow investors to tender their Par bonds, Discount bond or C bond for a 30-global bond issue or to purchase outright the new issue before June 3, provided the only spark of interest in an otherwise somnolent market, traders and analysts said.
Spreads of Brazil Bradys over U.S. Treasuries tightened about 5 basis points, traders said. The benchmark C bond added 1/4 to 79-1/2 bid.

Judging from the enthusiasm the roadshows generated last week, the new issue should succeed, said Marcelo Fleury, head of the Brazil desk at Garban Corp. Price talk ranged from 365 to 385 basis points over U.S. Treasuries.
The debt restructuring news not only helped lifting Brazil Bradys but also as boosted other Latin eurobonds, he said.
Unencumbered by collaterals, the 30-year Brazil global simplifies the arbitrage with other latin sovereign global issues, Fleury said.

Mexico's 30-year global, UMS 26, provided a point of reference for pricing the Brazil 30-year global, although Mexico's sovereign debt is rated higher at Ba2 by the Moody's and BB by Standard and Poor's than Brazil's at B1 and BB- status. UMS 26, rose 1/2 to bid at 111-1/2.
Argentina glb-17 also gained 3/8 to 109-3/4 bid.
But some investors appeared to be troubled by the fact that the C bond was not able to stay above 80 despite the rally, which appeared to puzzle some investors, Fleury noted.

Richard Segal, director of emerging market fixed income research at Santander Investments, said that other than the debt restructuring, Brazil had not delivered any strong fundamental news to soothe investors' worries about the country's troubling trade deficit.
He expected the new bond to fetch a spread of 375 to 380 basis points.
Among the Latin Bradys, Ecuador continued climbing, propelled by the upward momentum from the May 25 referendum, which showed strong popular support for President Fabian Alarcom, traders said.

Fidel Jaramillo, Ecuador's central bank chief said in New York on Monday that the economic team would stay intact and a fiscal austerity plan would be made public in the coming weeks. (( -- Nailene Chou Wiest - 212-859-1674))
